title: Four brothers at the lake
hook: one by one the brothers take from the yaksha's lake without asking, and why Hindus ask the earth's pardon each morning
carry: ask the earth's leave before you take

segments.voice: Yesterday: arani, the brahmin's fire-sticks, kept for Agni, and Nakula, who drank before he listened. Your line was agni carries the offering to the gods.
screen: `ARANI, KEPT FOR AGNI.` · `NAKULA DRANK, AND FELL.`

segments.voice: Nakula doesn't come back. Under the tree, his brothers wait, and wait, and Yudhishthira sends the next one. Sahadeva, go and find your brother, and bring water. So Sahadeva follows the cranes to the lake, and there is Nakula, lying on the bank. Sahadeva is grieving, and burning with thirst, and the voice speaks again, the same words. This lake is mine. Answer first. Back under the tree, three brothers are still waiting for water.
screen: `NAKULA DOESN'T COME BACK.` → `SAHADEVA GOES NEXT.` → `THE SAME VOICE, THE SAME WORDS.`

segments.voice: Sahadeva drinks, and falls beside his brother. Now Yudhishthira sends Arjuna, the great archer. Arjuna sees both twins dead and looks for an enemy. When the voice speaks, he shoots at it by ear alone. The voice answers, unhurt: your arrows can't touch me. Answer my questions, and then drink. Arjuna drinks, and falls. Then Bhima comes, the strong one, sure this is some spirit's work and ready to fight it, after a drink. The voice warns him too. He drinks, and falls. Thirst, grief, aim and strength, and not one of them asks. Listen again to what the voice said first: this lake is mine. In Hindu tradition the world is full of owners you can't see. Rivers are goddesses. Yakshas guard lakes and trees. The earth herself is Bhumi Devi, Mother Earth. So many Hindus begin the day with a short verse to her before their feet touch the floor, asking her to forgive them for stepping on her. Before a house is built, a bhoomi puja asks her leave. One way to hear the lake, then: the brothers didn't fail for lack of strength. They took without asking the owner. Four heroes of the Mahabharata lie on the shore. One brother is left.
screen: `SAHADEVA FALLS. ARJUNA SHOOTS.` · `NOT ONE OF THEM ASKS.` · `BHUMI DEVI, MOTHER EARTH.` · then, large: `THEY TOOK WITHOUT ASKING.`

segments.voice: Before you stand up from this, rest your fingertips on the floor, the way many Hindus do each morning. Feel the ground holding you up, as it has all day without being asked. Breathe in, and think of one thing you'll take from the earth today: water, food, a place to walk. If you pray, ask Bhumi Devi's pardon and thank her in your own words; if not, simply thank the ground, then touch your fingers to your heart.
Yaksha, the unseen spirit who owns the lake and asks before anyone may drink. Four brothers bring thirst, grief, aim and strength, and none of them asks the owner. Today's word.
Your line: ask the earth's leave before you take. Thirst, grief, aim and strength all came up short. Day eight hundred two, done.

howItsDone: In the epic, the four brothers fall one by one before Yudhishthira arrives, each warned by the same voice in the same words. Many Hindus touch the floor on waking and ask Mother Earth's pardon, and a bhoomi puja asks her leave before building.
